entries.text: My cousin swears the {name} tore a caravan apart looking for one stolen egg
Somebody's selling {al:bodyPlan} egg under the counter. Whoever it is, I hope they can run
They say it {f:behaviour} now, ever since someone robbed its lair
Never buy an egg off a stranger. Last fool who did, the parent came calling
The thief's still out there. So is the {name}, and it's got the scent
Saw the stolen egg on a stall in Sigil, priced like a small castle
The fey took its young, they say, and left a pinecone in its place
Pirates took its young. Now every ship out of port gets followed
Touch a {name} and your children are born with its eyes. Or so Gran says
It was a person once, cursed for lying, the way I heard it
My uncle wounded one out in {the:habitat}. Hasn't slept a night since
They say the curse breaks if someone shows it kindness. Nobody's volunteered
Why do you think it {f:behaviour}? Curses make a creature do strange things
Salt your door and never say its name after dark. That's all I'll say
The ones it kills get up again. Seen it myself, near enough
Its kind made a deal once. The other party's coming to collect, and soon
Somebody holds a contract on every {name} alive. Find the paper, own the beasts
Folk say it {f:behaviour} because the deal says so. Terms are terms
My gran swore you can bargain with one, if you bring the right price
Whoever wrote the pact is still alive, and still owed
Ask any tiefling: a devil holds the deed, and devils never forget a debt
It lost a wager with the fey. Now it pays in riddles, poor thing
Someone it trusted sold it out. It remembers faces, you know
The one who betrayed it lives in comfort now. Not for long, I'd wager
Used to eat from a keeper's hand, that one. Then the keeper brought hunters
It won't come near folk any more. Can't blame it, after what was done
Ever wonder why it {f:behaviour}? Betrayal changes a creature
A lord up the valley got rich off its hide. The {name} wants the rest back
The drow sold it out. Now drow patrols go missing, and nobody weeps
Last of its kind, supposedly. My brother saw one in {the:habitat} last spring
Scholars pay silver for any sighting of a {name}. Most are made up
They're all gone, they say. Funny, then, that something still {f:behaviour}
An old map shows where the last one went to ground. Map's for sale, of course
Hunters swear there's one left, {f:scale}, deep in {the:habitat}
A salvage crew found its bones. Then the bones walked off
Went through a portal and never came out. Or came out somewhere worse
It's awake again. The birds knew before we did
It slept for a hundred years. Now it {f:behaviour}, and it's in a mood
Something woke it, and I'd bet my boots it wants something
My neighbour heard it calling a name in the night. Not a name anyone knows
Dead ones don't stay dead, not this kind. Mark my words
The ice cracked on the lake last week, and something walked out of it
The forge fire went green, and the {name} came out of it purring
It's guarding something. Nothing sits that still without a reason
Get past the {name} and there's treasure. Nobody's got past the {name}
My grandad said it was set to watch a door. Nobody knows what's behind it
Leave it be. If it ever stops guarding, we'll find out why it was there
It {f:behaviour}, sure, but only near that old ruin. It's on duty
An angel put it there. You don't argue with an angel's watchdog
The crypt it sits on is full of old lords. Rich ones
The old songs name it. When it comes down from {the:habitat}, a king falls
There's a prophecy about the {name}. Everybody's got a different version
A seer told my sister it would come this year. My sister's moved away
When it {f:behaviour} three nights running, that's the sign. It did last week
Some cult wants the prophecy to happen. Others are paying good coin to stop it
The chosen one's meant to ride it. Good luck with that, I say
The skalds have started singing the last verse. They never sing the last verse
